h.strategy: Borrow interaction patterns from other empirical sciences: epistasis in genetics (the effect of one mutation depends on genetic background, and beneficial mutations help fitter backgrounds less), diminishing returns in economics, and redundancy in engineered systems. Translate each pattern into a concrete conditional hypothesis about how an edit's effect varies with the parent configuration. Favor predictions that a practitioner thinking only mechanistically would get wrong, especially background-dependent sign changes and weaker gains in already-strong parents. Use conditions that many parents satisfy. In the flaw step, discard analogies that do not transfer and keep only those with a plausible general reason to hold.

hyps.why: A skip shortcut into node 3 already provides a strong parallel path, so an extra conv on 1->3 is redundant.
Filling an empty edge with a conv gains more than upgrading an existing op.
If node 1 receives no input, edge 2 is dead, so the conv edit is wasted.
Replacing none with a conv adds a whole new path, gaining more than swapping an existing op.
A conv upstream on 0->1->3 gives the downstream conv richer features to refine.
If node 1 receives no input, edge 4 carries nothing, so the upgrade is wasted.
Filling an empty edge with a conv gains more than upgrading an existing op.
Replacing identity with conv gains less than replacing none because skip already supplies most of the benefit.
When a strong conv route into node 3 already exists, the shortcut's marginal benefit shrinks.
Replacing skip with conv gains less than filling an empty edge or replacing weaker ops, because skip is already a good op.
